Inside you’ll find wider 19-inch wheels, upgraded suspension and brakes, carbon-fibre trim, and the same 400 hp twin-turbo 3.0-litre V6 as the Q50 Red Sport 400. In this video we dive deep into the specs, craftsmanship and future implications for both Infiniti and Nissan. We break down what this means for the brand’s performance halo, the rare collector angle of the 400R Limited, and how the upcoming 2027 rear-wheel-drive sedan may resurrect the Q50 nameplate. Whether you’re a driving enthusiast, luxury-sedan fan or collector, this one is especially for you. Don’t miss our full breakdown of the tech, the market context and how it connects back to Infiniti’s SUV-only strategy and its plan to re-enter the sedan world.
